active.title: Validate balance-transparent model cleanup
active.objective: Human-listen the same-balance RAW vs CLEAN Ptitsa rerender, with RAW/CLEAN/REMOVED per-source checks especially for both vocals, before making model cleanup the studio baseline.

live-soundcheck-v2: Studio-derived one-hypothesis live decision engine added
Masking action now requires measured overlap instead of legacy dominance heuristic
Live decision tests wired into CI and passed in workflow run 35833133811
studio-perceptual-v21: Perceptual Critic now has an explicit one-hypothesis candidate acceptance gate
Target-direction and collateral-regression tests added; focused perceptual tests passed 6/6
Artifact Critic was revised to be Nyquist-safe and to use a click-rate-specific regression tolerance
Full CI subsequently progressed through later studio regressions instead of the former Artifact Critic failure
studio-editing-small-sample: Full Tests run 35837914007 failed identically on Python 3.10/3.11/3.12 because robust_outliers disabled all passages shorter than eight events
Short-passage policy revised: six events can expose an extreme level defect; fewer than six remain diagnose-only
A 0.25 dB robust-scale floor prevents tiny low-variance performance differences from becoming false outliers
Regression coverage added for an obvious six-event defect, a stable six-event phrase, and a five-event diagnose-only phrase
studio-editing-click-candidate: The synthetic one-sample click creates two adjacent derivative spikes; the old detector compared each spike against the other and suppressed both
click_candidates now clusters adjacent supra-threshold derivative samples, compares the cluster against activity outside it and rejects broad transient runs
Regression tests cover impulse, step discontinuity, broad ramp and smooth periodic signal
Tests run 35852601258 progressed past click_candidate to a later guitar-director failure after 344 passed and 1 skipped on Python 3.11
studio-guitar-wall-nyquist: Tests run 35852601258 exposed a separate wall_layer failure: a fixed 9 kHz band edge exceeded Nyquist in the 1 kHz reduced-rate fixture
The wall-layer filter now caps its upper edge below Nyquist and fails closed to silence when the intended band cannot exist
The fixture now contains an in-band guitar-like sine instead of DC, so it actually tests dense-section wall energy
Later Tests run 35853333095 cleared the guitar regression and reached mastering streaming after 672 passed and 2 skipped on Python 3.11
studio-cleanup-checkpointing: Original sequential Ptitsa cleanup run 35828150231 reached the 180-minute workflow timeout and was cancelled before render/upload
Cleanup workflow refactored into 11 per-stem matrix jobs with max-parallel 6
Each completed stem uploads a durable checkpoint: cleaned WAV, RAW/CLEAN/REMOVED MP3 previews and JSON residual metrics
Replacement run 35846566268 completed all 11 per-stem jobs successfully and completed the final full-mix render
Final artifact ptitsa-full-model-cleanup-mix id 10746216442 contains Ptitsa_ModelClean_FullMix_50pct.wav, 320 kbps MP3 and validation previews

Objective residual screen: NIKITA_VOX removed/raw = -6.62 dB and VALERA_VOX = -7.62 dB, while the non-vocal cleaned sources range from about -29.38 dB to -52.49 dB removed/raw; vocals therefore require especially careful human A/B before acceptance
studio-cleanup-balance-transparency: User rejected the first cleaned full mix because instrument balance was destroyed, so cleanup and mixing responsibilities are now explicitly separated

Balance-transparent rerender workflow commit 10476989915e54eded8f6c6c1055cef2fd6c8fd3 completed successfully in run 35859737710; artifact ptitsa-balance-transparent-rerender id 10749861292 contains same-balance RAW and CLEAN WAV/MP3 plus validation JSON
All 11 CLEAN sources matched RAW length exactly: 11421900 frames each and zero sample drift
Active-RMS matching passed the 0.05 dB gate on every processed source; maximum absolute post-match delta was about 0.00000051 dB
Non-vocal level corrections were <= 0.019 dB, while NIKITA_VOX required +4.781 dB and VALERA_VOX +3.502 dB, explaining a major source of the earlier balance collapse
Same-balance full mixes measured -20.575 LUFS RAW vs -20.549 LUFS CLEAN, with peaks -3.128 vs -3.000 dBFS; machine transparency passed, subjective acceptance remains human-only
Cleanup contract updated in commit 6385478b1309ba1076a4569df9ada53c55f7aefc: time/length align, active-level match within 0.05 dB, preserve gain/pan/automation until Mixing Director
studio-mastering-numpy2: Tests run 35853333095 reached tests/test_mastering_streaming.py after 672 passed and 2 skipped on Python 3.11, then failed because NumPy 2 removed np.trapz in mastering analyzer
Analyzer compatibility fix cf19fea72b8a062b00d311b6663be9357dcd6cb1 switched to np.trapezoid with legacy np.trapz fallback
The next matrix run 35865011220 progressed further to 892 passed and 2 skipped on Python 3.12, exposing the same obsolete np.trapz call in musical_critic.py
Musical Critic now reuses the shared NumPy-compatible integration helper; fix commit 6eca08d37badafb6ae838fbe387158036e873fa9
Full Tests run 35865456706 passed on Python 3.10, 3.11 and 3.12; Stem Offline Test 35865011214 also passed on the analyzer fix

blockers.step: Same-balance RAW vs CLEAN full-mix A/B, then per-source RAW/CLEAN/REMOVED checks where needed
blockers.note: Machine balance-transparency checks passed. Subjective timbre/artifact acceptance is still required, especially for NIKITA_VOX and VALERA_VOX because their cleanup outputs needed +4.781 dB and +3.502 dB level restoration.

history.note: Full multitrack download succeeded; neural cleanup was computing.
Studio-derived live decision engine tests are now part of CI and passed.
Added perceptual candidate acceptance and collateral regression guards.
Artifact Critic attempted a 6-14 kHz bandpass at 8 kHz sample rate and click-rate regression used an unsuitable generic 0.08 threshold.
Made Artifact Critic Nyquist-safe and click regression sensitivity metric-specific; later CI progressed to an editing-performance failure.
All three Python jobs stopped at test_editing_performance: a clearly defective sixth event was suppressed solely by the hard len<8 guard.
Lowered the evidence floor to six events and added regression coverage; subsequent CI reached test_click_candidate after 295 passing tests on Python 3.11.
The sequential CPU cleanup hit the workflow 180-minute limit. Final render, MP3 encoding and artifact upload were skipped, so no usable checkpoint survived.
Split 11 model-cleaned sources into independent matrix jobs; every source checkpoint and the final full cleaned mix completed successfully.

All RAW/CLEAN/REMOVED previews are available. Vocal removed/raw RMS is much stronger (-6.62/-7.62 dB) than non-vocal sources (about -29.38 to -52.49 dB), so vocals are explicitly high-risk for over-cleaning until listened to.
Clustered adjacent derivative spikes and added impulse/step/ramp/sine guards; CI progressed past click_candidate and stopped later at guitar wall_layer after 344 passes on Python 3.11.
Made the wall-layer filter Nyquist-safe and corrected the reduced-rate fixture; later CI progressed through 672 passes before a mastering compatibility failure.

CLEAN sources were length-aligned and active-RMS matched to RAW under the frozen mix recipe. All 11 passed <=0.05 dB active-level delta; vocals required +4.781/+3.502 dB restoration. Same-balance RAW/CLEAN A/B rendered for human acceptance.
Cleanup is now explicitly prohibited from changing mix balance; gain/pan/automation belong to Mixing Director after cleanup acceptance.
Analyzer was made NumPy-2-compatible; the next matrix cleared mastering streaming and then found the same removed np.trapz API in Musical Critic after 892 passes on Python 3.12.
Musical Critic now reuses the shared integration helper. Full Tests passed on Python 3.10, 3.11 and 3.12.
